title: NPCI Builds an AI Arm: NTSL Takes On Tech Beyond UPI
description: NPCI has set up NPCI Tech Solutions, its fourth subsidiary, led by CTO Vishal Kanvaty, to build AI, blockchain and GCC capability beyond UPI's payments core.
tldr: NPCI announced NPCI Tech Solutions Limited (NTSL) on November 4, 2026, a wholly owned subsidiary focused on artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital financial infrastructure and GCC services.
Vishal Kanvaty, NPCI's chief technology officer, has been appointed managing director and chief executive of NTSL.
NTSL is the group's fourth subsidiary and will also run technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform and other digital public infrastructure programmes.
NPCI has not published a product roadmap, model or hiring plan, so this is capability-building rather than a launched AI product.

sections.heading: A fourth subsidiary, and not one about UPI
paragraphs: On Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the National Payments Corporation of India announced a wholly owned subsidiary called NPCI Tech Solutions Limited (NTSL), which will act as the technology and innovation arm of the NPCI group. The Hindu reported the formation on Friday morning, noting that the new company will focus on artificial intelligence, blockchain and digital financial infrastructure, along with Global Capability Centre services. NPCI operates India's retail payments and settlement systems, including the Unified Payments Interface.

NTSL is the group's fourth wholly owned subsidiary, after NPCI International Payments Limited, which handles UPI and RuPay abroad, NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited, which runs bill payments, and NPCI BHIM Services Limited, which runs the BHIM app. Business Standard reported that the subsidiary was set up with approval from the NPCI board and the Reserve Bank of India. One structural detail stands out: when Business Standard first reported the plan in January 2026, it noted that NTSL would not be a Section 8 company like the other three, placing it outside the not-for-profit structure the rest of the group uses.

sections.heading: What NTSL has actually been asked to build
paragraphs: NPCI's brief is deliberately wider than payments. According to the corporation's statement, NTSL will build capabilities across emerging technology domains and support the expansion of the group's technology initiatives. Concretely, it will provide technology services for eKYC Setu and the Unified Ticketing Platform, and support other Digital Public Infrastructure programmes, The Hindu and Medianama reported. Both systems sit close to the infrastructure that fintechs and state transport bodies build on.

The January reporting adds a useful framing. A person familiar with the plan told Business Standard that NTSL is not meant to compete with vendors: "It is not the objective to compete with vendors. The focus is on scaling up technology solutions and playing the role of central infrastructure." At that stage the paid-up capital was recorded at five lakh rupees against authorised capital of ten lakh rupees, which reads more like an experimentation vehicle than a large operating company. Ajay Kumar Choudhary, NPCI's non-executive chairman, said at the Global Fintech Fest 2025 that he expected NTSL to become "a cradle for tech innovation in India".

sections.heading: The scale any AI work here would sit on
paragraphs: Whatever NTSL builds will run on top of an unusually large transaction base. UPI processed a record 25.47 billion transactions worth 31.53 lakh crore rupees in October 2026, according to NPCI data reported by Mint and Entrackr. That works out to about 822 million transactions a day, and average daily value crossed one lakh crore rupees for the first time at roughly 1,01,707 crore rupees. Volume grew 23 per cent and value 16 per cent over October 2025.

The shape of that traffic matters. A HaiPay analysis of NPCI's monthly statistics put the average UPI transaction at 1,238 rupees in October, down from 1,318 rupees a year earlier, while the number of banks live on UPI rose to 758 from 683. More small payments across more institutions is exactly the profile where machine learning earns its place: fraud scoring, dispute handling, reconciliation and capacity planning all get harder as ticket sizes fall and volumes rise. NPCI's monthly figures do not break transactions down by purpose, so they cannot show how much of October's growth came from festive spending.

sections.heading: The engineer now running it
paragraphs: NPCI has put its own chief technology officer in charge. Vishal Kanvaty has been appointed managing director and chief executive of NTSL. He has been with NPCI for nearly a decade, having joined in 2017 and risen to CTO in April 2023. Before that he led the market innovation portfolio, and NPCI said the platforms he developed and commercialised now form part of NTSL's focus areas. Medianama reported that these market innovation platforms will move under NTSL's remit.

Dilip Asbe, NPCI's managing director and chief executive, framed the subsidiary around the technology shift. "As we look ahead, advancements in Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technologies are creating new possibilities across digital infrastructure and financial services," he said in the release. "NTSL has been established to focus on these opportunities and further strengthen the NPCI Group's technology capabilities." Reuters noted that the move comes as India pushes to advance AI research and development, particularly in banking and financial services.

sections.heading: What it means for builders, students and businesses
paragraphs: For fintechs and startups, the useful signal is the list of systems NTSL will run. Identity verification, transit ticketing and shared DPI components are costly for a small company to build and maintain alone. If a central body scales them, the cost of launching a payments-adjacent product falls, and the stated intention not to compete with vendors leaves room for private companies to build on top rather than against it. Any founder working on KYC, ticketing or payment operations has a reason to track what NTSL ships next.

For students and working professionals, the GCC services line is the part to watch, because it points to capability being built inside India rather than bought from outside. A public infrastructure body hiring for AI and blockchain engineering is a different employer from a services firm: the work is on systems used at national scale, and the skills transfer is in reliability rather than client delivery. The honest caveat is that NPCI has published no roadmap, no model, no hiring numbers and no timeline. The announcement establishes an institution and a mandate. What the AI work looks like, and whether it touches UPI's core, is still to be disclosed.

faq.q: What is NPCI Tech Solutions Limited?
faq.a: NTSL is a wholly owned subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India, announced on November 4, 2026. It serves as the group's technology and innovation arm, working on artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital financial infrastructure and Global Capability Centre services, and running technology for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform and other digital public infrastructure programmes.

faq.q: Will NTSL change how UPI works for users?
faq.a: Nothing announced so far changes UPI for users. UPI continues to be operated by NPCI, and NTSL is positioned as a technology and innovation arm that builds capabilities beyond the core payments mandate. NPCI has not published any product, model or timeline that would alter the consumer UPI experience.

faq.q: Why does a payments body need a separate AI company?
faq.a: NPCI's stated reason is that emerging technologies are opening new possibilities across digital infrastructure and financial services, and a dedicated arm lets the group build that capability outside its core payments operations. The subsidiary was set up with NPCI board and Reserve Bank of India approval, and unlike the group's other three subsidiaries it is not structured as a Section 8 company.
